title: Log source (log generator; Filebeat later) delivers log lines to Kafka
objective: Check that the current CRAN log source, the log generator that simulates the mirror until Filebeat is deployed, delivers well-formed access-log lines to the raw topic. It tests the interface (topic, line format) that Filebeat must also meet, not Filebeat itself.
steps: Read the end offsets of cran_mirror_logs, wait 10 s, read them again.
Read a sample of messages and match each against the Apache common log format.
expected: At least 20 new messages in 10 s; every sampled message is a valid common-log line.
actual: 39 messages in 10 s; 200/200 sampled lines are valid common-log lines.

title: Platform initialisation: topics, schemas, HDFS directories
objective: Check that deploy/init.sh created everything the acquisition modules write to.
steps: Describe the Kafka topics.
List the Schema Registry subjects.
List the HDFS raw and clean directories.
expected: Six topics with 3 partitions, three Avro subjects and eight HDFS directories exist.
actual: 6 topics (3 partitions), 3 Avro subjects and 8 HDFS data directories exist.

title: GitHub poller unit tests (mocked HTTP)
objective: Check the poller logic offline: ETags, rate limits, scheduling, retries, watch-list, Kafka sink, state.
steps: Run pytest -m 'not live' in poller/.
expected: All tests pass.
actual: pytest -m 'not live': 107 passed, 5 deselected in 3.56s.

title: GitHub poller live tests (real API)
objective: Check the poller against the real GitHub Events API with the project token.
steps: Run pytest -m live in poller/ with GITHUB_TOKEN set.
expected: All live tests pass.
actual: pytest -m live (real GitHub API): 5 passed, 107 deselected in 7.74s.

title: Watch-list build from crantogit and publication to Kafka
objective: Check that the watch-list is built from crantogit.csv and published to github_repo_list.
steps: Read /data/watchlist.csv from the poller container as a DataFrame.
Validate columns, tiers and endpoints.
Read github_repo_list and compare the rows of the latest build.
expected: Valid watch-list; the latest build published exactly the rows of the file.
actual: 2627 watch-list rows ({2: 1983, 1: 644}), all published to github_repo_list.

title: GitHub events reach Kafka with the documented format
objective: Check the structure, keys and package matching of the events written by the poller.
steps: Read all messages of github_repo_updates.
Check the keys, mandatory fields, track values and package matching.
expected: Key = repository name; every message has the documented fields; events are matched to CRAN packages.
actual: 4814 events in Kafka, keys correct, 3811 matched to CRAN packages.

title: API limit handling: conditional requests and quota
objective: Check from the poller's own request log that ETags are used and the quota is respected.
steps: Read the request log of the poller (requests-*.jsonl) as a DataFrame.
Count polls by HTTP status.
Check rate-limit flags and the remaining quota.
expected: Both 200 and 304 responses occur; no rate limit; remaining quota stays above the reserve.
actual: 588 polls, statuses {200: 554, 304: 34}; no rate limit; minimum remaining quota 4303.

title: Poller restart does not duplicate events
objective: Check that the poller keeps its state (ETags, written event ids) across a restart.
steps: Record the event ids in github_repo_updates.
Restart the poller container and wait for several poll rounds.
Check in the poller's request log that it polled again and that polls after the restart got 304 (ETags kept).
Check that no event id occurs twice and earlier events are still present.
expected: Polls after the restart; some answered 304; no duplicate event ids.
actual: 214 polls after the restart ({200: 205, 304: 9}); 8031 distinct events, 0 duplicates.

title: Valid CRAN log lines are parsed into the clean topic
objective: Check the parsing of the Flink log job for valid lines.
steps: Produce six valid test lines to cran_mirror_logs.
Read them from cran_mirror_logs_clean (Avro).
Compare every field with the input.
expected: All six lines arrive with correct fields; '-' size becomes null.
actual: All 6 valid test lines reached cran_mirror_logs_clean with correct fields; '-' size became null.

title: Invalid CRAN log lines are rejected with a reason
objective: Check that invalid lines are kept in the bad zone and never reach the clean data.
steps: Produce six invalid lines (garbage, status 999, method FOO, +1 day, -30 days, offset +0200).
Read /data/raw/cran_mirror_logs_bad as a DataFrame.
Compare reject_reason with the expectation.
Check the clean topic.
expected: Each line is in the bad zone with the expected reason and absent from the clean topic.
actual: 6/6 invalid lines were rejected with the expected reject_reason and none reached the clean topic.

title: Package downloads are extracted from the clean log
objective: Check the download extraction job: package, version, artifact type, target system, outcome.
steps: Use the valid test lines of FP-01 (source, macOS, Windows, a 404, PACKAGES.rds, an HTML page).
Read cran_mirror_package_downloads (Avro).
Compare the derived fields; check the skipped requests.
expected: Four downloads with correct fields (404 = FAILURE); the two non-package requests are skipped.
actual: 4/4 package requests were extracted correctly (source, macos, windows, 404 as FAILURE); 2 non-downloads skipped.

title: GitHub events: mapping and deduplication
objective: Check the GitHub Flink job: field extraction, nullable fields and removal of repeated event ids.
steps: Produce a ReleaseEvent twice and a PushEvent without organisation to github_repo_updates.
Read github_repo_updates_clean (Avro).
Compare the fields; count the occurrences of the repeated event.
expected: The repeated event appears once; fields are mapped; missing organisation is null.
actual: Duplicate event kept once; release_tag, ref, packages and nullable org_login mapped correctly.

title: Invalid GitHub records are rejected with a reason
objective: Check the validation rules of the GitHub job.
steps: Produce five invalid records (30 days old, track 'other', not JSON, no repo name, invalid timestamp).
Read /data/raw/github_repo_updates_bad as a DataFrame.
Compare reject_reason; check the clean topic.
expected: Each record is in the bad zone with the expected reason and absent from the clean topic.
actual: 5/5 invalid GitHub events were rejected with the expected reject_reason.

title: Raw records are stored unchanged
objective: Check that the raw zone keeps every input record byte for byte, valid or not.
steps: Read the text files of /data/raw/cran_mirror_logs and /data/raw/github_repo_updates.
Look for each injected record.
expected: All injected records are present unchanged.
actual: All 12 injected log lines and 8 injected GitHub records are stored unchanged in the raw zone.

title: Schema conformance and value constraints
objective: Check that the Parquet files have the columns of the Avro schemas and that values satisfy the constraints Avro cannot express. Decoding the Kafka messages is only a sanity check: the jobs write them with the registered schema.
steps: Decode every message of the three derived topics with the schema from the registry.
Compare the Parquet columns with the Avro fields.
Check status range, methods, allowed values.
expected: Everything decodes; columns match; all constraints hold.
actual: All three clean topics decode with the registry schema; Parquet columns match; value constraints hold.

title: No duplicate GitHub events in the clean data
objective: Check that deduplication on event_id works on the live data.
steps: Count distinct event ids in the clean topic and in the Parquet files.
Compare with the raw topic.
expected: No event id occurs twice in the clean data.
actual: 2905 clean events, 0 duplicates (topic and Parquet); 1 repeated raw records were dropped.

title: Completeness: no record is lost between raw, clean and rejected
objective: Check that raw = clean + rejected for the CRAN logs, and that Kafka and HDFS agree.
steps: Stop the producers and wait until the Flink consumer lag is 0 and the files are finalised.
Count the raw topic, raw text, clean topic, clean Parquet and bad Parquet.
expected: raw = clean + rejected; topic counts equal file counts.
actual: 2462 raw lines = 2456 clean + 6 rejected; Kafka and HDFS counts agree.

title: Partitioning by event time
objective: Check that Parquet files are in the dt/hr directory of the record's time.
steps: Read the Parquet datasets and compare dt and hr with event_ts (arrival_ts for rejects).
expected: Every row is in the correct partition.
actual: All Parquet rows are in the partition matching their event time (rejected lines: arrival time).

title: Keys and partition locality
objective: Check that records of one package or repository stay in one partition.
steps: Group the downloads topic by package_name and the GitHub topic by repo_name.
Count partitions per key.
expected: Exactly one partition per key; key equals the field.
actual: Records with the same package_name / repo_name always go to the same partition, so their order is kept.

title: Reject accounting
objective: Check that rejections happen only for the documented reasons and only where expected.
steps: Count the rejected CRAN lines by reason and compare them with the injected invalid lines.
Count the rejected GitHub records by reason.
expected: CRAN rejects are exactly the injected ones; GitHub reasons are documented, stale history is rejected.
actual: CRAN: 6 rejects, all of them injected test lines. GitHub: 2219 rejects ({'stale_timestamp': 2215, 'invalid_track': 1, 'unparseable': 1, 'missing_field': 1, 'invalid_timestamp': 1}), 2905 clean events.

title: Event-time plausibility of the clean data
objective: Check the time bounds the ingest jobs promise.
steps: Compute event_ts - arrival_ts (CRAN) and fetched_ts - event_ts (GitHub) over all clean rows.
expected: CRAN: -7 d to +5 min; GitHub: 0 to about 7 d.
actual: All clean records satisfy the event-time bounds enforced by the ingest jobs.
